fields.title: Allow task add from a plain terminal
fields.description: Allow task add from a plain shell with no Claude session through an explicit bypass, and list that bypass among the error message's fix options.
fields.context: Today the E-1401 attribution gate in event_bridge.emit_event() refuses task.add from a plain shell with no resolvable session, and --force does not bypass it (the gate fires before --force is consulted).

fields.title: Stop task update --text from creating a worktree
fields.description: Stop task update --text from creating a worktree before the task is claimed, storing the plan in the main checkout for claim to copy in later.
fields.analysis:
Change the trigger from 'no worktree exists' to 'task has been claimed (status=in_progress) OR has sessions.active_task_id binding'.

Until claimed, --text sets the DB text and writes the plan into the main checkout's .endless/plans/ for later claim to copy in.

fields.title: Include the worktree slug in sandbox directory names
fields.description: Include the worktree slug in sandbox directory names so each worktree of a task gets its own sandbox database instead of sharing one.
fields.context:
Today sandbox dir name is 'worktree-e-{task_id}' (worktree_cmd.py), built from task_id only - the worktree dir's optional slug suffix is collapsed away.

Multiple worktrees for the same task (e.g., one for production work, one for testing) share a single sandbox and conflate their DB state.

Mike's case: a testing worktree may have different DB needs than the non-testing version.

fields.title: Drop the worktree- prefix from sandbox directory names
fields.description: Drop the worktree- prefix from sandbox directory names so each matches its worktree directory's name exactly.
fields.context: Sandbox dir names follow 'worktree-e-{task_id}' convention from worktree_cmd.py;
fields.analysis:
the 'worktree-' prefix exists for disambiguation against other sandbox kinds that never materialized.

Cleaner listing, simpler mental model.
